facts.description: Use NIMS 2017 and identify all four official command-and-coordination structures.
JIS is the fourth structure and operates across ICS, EOCs, and MAC Group; JIC manages JIS activities; MACS is only an umbrella term if used.
facts.expected_value: Four peer structures; JIS cross-cutting; JIC subordinate/center; MACS umbrella only

facts.description: ICS handles on-scene tactical incident management, command/objectives, operational organization, and Unified Command when authorities share responsibility.
facts.source: FEMA slides 21, 24 and related command-and-coordination content
facts.expected_value: On-scene tactical command and operational organization, including Unified Command concept

facts.description: EOC provides off-scene support to incident command, on-scene personnel, and other EOCs without taking tactical command.
Universal EOC functions are distinguished from variable organization and activation examples.
MAC Group participation and decision roles include senior administrators/executives, supported participant categories, strategic policy, scarce resources, and cooperative decisions.
MAC Group does not command incidents or field tactics and does not replace operations, coordination, or dispatch.
expected_value: Does not replace operations, coordination, or dispatch

facts.description: JIS integrates incident information and public affairs for public and stakeholders using the source quality standard.
expected_value: Integrates incident information and public affairs

facts.description: JIS supports all three other structures; JIC manages JIS activities; activity examples are source-grounded.
Eligible feedback is ranked by distinct eligible-session prevalence, then response count, then recency.
facts.expected_value: Join sheets; eligible submitted participant surveys from completed Spring 2026 Partner Orientation sessions; rank by distinct sessions

expected_value: MAC policy/resource decisions versus operational command
EOC common functions versus one fixed organization/activation model
JIS public scope, audience, and information standards versus internal/EOC-only communications

facts.description: Exactly three misconception-plus-correction notes without quotes, counts, unanswered questions, or a fourth topic.
Four concurrent actions map to ICS/UC, EOC, MAC Group, and JIS through JIC with their detailed roles and boundaries preserved.
FEMA NIMS 2017 attribution is included and off-scope or unsupported additions are excluded.
facts.expected_value: FEMA NIMS 2017 source line; no active 2008 comparison, Planning P, detailed workflows, activation table, detailed org charts, course sequence, contacts, or local logo

calibration_note: Grounded score-2 thresholds require complete multi-part source synthesis. The checklist does not use typography, layout, aesthetic, overlap, clipping, or other general visual-quality conditions; the unchanged single visual VQA remains responsible for those judgments.
